aline (security): Heads-up — prepping KMS design doc for Redwood Private. Quick architecture Q: control plane vs data-plane CMKs — do we want separate customer-managed CMKs or allow a single CMK per tenant?

mike-r (infra): Separate CMKs. Control-plane key scope is smaller (credentials, certs, signing), dataplane CMK wraps DEKs used for blobs/checkpoints. Different rotation cadence and audit helps isolate blast radius.

jaspreet (eng-ml): Agree. Dataplane perf note: unwrapping DEKs on every request kills latency. We need a DEK cache with TTL + invalidation on rekey. Suggest default TTL 15m and per-pod LRU capped by memory.

olivia (platform): Proposed pattern: BYOK allowed for both planes; default Redwood-managed keys named alias/redwood/private/{env}/{tenant}/{role}. Use grants for runtime decrypt/reencrypt by our service role rather than giving long-term IAM key perms.

aline (security): Quick Qs: KMS grants vs key policy vs IAM role — which should we prefer for our service accounts? And should we enforce encryption context to bind requests to tenant_id?

mike-r (infra): Use key policy to grant account-level admin, but use grants for runtime operations. Grants are revocable and faster than changing policies. Always require EncryptionContext (tenant_id, region) to mitigate cross-tenant rewraps.

jaspreet (eng-ml): Example grant I would create during bootstrap: 
```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id alias/redwood-dataplane-cmk \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-dataplane \
  --operations Decrypt,ReEncryptFrom,ReEncryptTo \
  --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"tenant_id":"TENANT123"}
```
This limits runtime to that tenant context.

olivia (platform): Rotation plan: staged rewrap. Create new CMK, then run tenant-scoped rewrap job that reads ciphertext DEKs, calls ReEncrypt (or Decrypt+GenerateDataKey), writes back ciphertext pointing to new CMK. Keep old CMK Enabled until all tenants rewrapped and retention window passed. Tag DEKs `rekey:pending`/`rekey:done`.

aline (security): DEK cache invalidation: how do we avoid serving with stale DEKs during rotation?

jaspreet (eng-ml): Cache 15m default. On rotation we emit a cache-invalidation event via control-plane pub/sub for affected tenants. Workers drop cached DEKs immediately and fetch new ciphertext/unwrapped DEK on next request. Also add version metadata on DEK records so mismatch is detectable.

mike-r (infra): Fallback strategy if KMS unreachable: node-level emergency mode that switches to a software-encrypted wrapping key derived from an HSM-rooted secret with strict gating. This is for brief outages only and must produce an auditable event. Not enabled by default.

aline (security): BYOK (customer-owned CMK) considerations: customers want to supply CMKs from their account. Any extra controls needed?

mike-r (infra): For BYOK require a customer key policy that explicitly allows our service principal (example below) and include kms:ViaService + aws:SourceVpc condition so only calls from customer VPC endpoints are honored. Also require EncryptionContext enforcement. We'll provide a template during onboarding.

jaspreet (eng-ml): Implementation flow (dataplane DEK):
1) Service requests `GenerateDataKey` with `EncryptionContext={tenant_id}`
2) KMS returns `Plaintext` + `CiphertextBlob`
3) Service uses `Plaintext` to encrypt object, immediately zeroes it from memory, and stores `CiphertextBlob` in DB/base64.
This avoids storing plaintext anywhere.

olivia (platform): Monitoring & audit: enable CloudTrail KMS events, forward to S3 bucket + Athena for queries. Create CloudWatch alarms for spikes in `Decrypt` or `GenerateDataKey` error rates. Require retention policy (e.g., 7 years) for enterprise customers. Also enable AWS Config rules for `kms-key-rotation-enabled` where applicable.

kms-bot: KMS alert: DecryptErrors spike for alias/redwood-dataplane-cmk at 1948654310 — auto-ticket created.

aline (security): Filed internal ticket SEC-4721 to track rotation/re-readiness. Assigning: @mike-r infra plan, @olivia runbook & BYOK template, @jaspreet DEK cache & invalidation hooks.

mike-r (infra): I'll sketch the key-policy + grant examples and post in #eng-security tomorrow with sample IAM snippets and recommended alias naming.

jaspreet (eng-ml): I'll prototype the cache invalidation hook and run a quick benchmark for unwrap latency at different DEK TTLs.

olivia (platform): I'll draft onboarding doc and BYOK key policy template, plus dry-run rewrap tool with `--simulate` flag for safety.

aline (security): Follow-ups for design doc: must include encryption context enforcement, CloudTrail + S3 retention 7 years for enterprise, grant revocation playbook, and HSM-software fallback checklist.

mike-r (infra): Noted. Will incorporate.

aline (security): Closing for now — will update SEC-4721 with next steps and timelines. :thumbsup:
